pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/42335

This PR will: 
1. [x] Add MSBuild item `<SupportedPlatform Include="browser" />` for the browser targets so that we could see warning if it accesses and API unsupported on browser.
2. [x] Tried to resolve warnings/errors that currently exist with the annotations that have been made. Mostly suppressed them as they are unconditionally accessing APIs having assembly-level Unsupported on browser attribute

The warnings found attached [unsupported browser warnings.txt](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/files/5372839/unsupported.browser.warnings.txt)

> PortableThreadPoolEventSource.cs

> TimerQueue.Portable.cs

This file should not be used, there is browser specific implementation in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/mono/netcore/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Threading/TimerQueue.Browser.Mono.cs

Why complicate the code to ifdef it out?  If IsThreadStartSupported is false for the relevant builds, the linker will trim it all away, anyway.

Those do not need an issue, safe to suppress scenarios, improved the suppression comments

issue_context.title: Blazor developers get warnings when they call APIs that aren't available on WebAssembly
issue_context.body:
For #41087, we annotated many APIs with `[UnsupportedOSPlatform("browser")]`, which will allow the Platform Compatibility Analyzer to provide customers with warnings when calling APIs that are unsupported on browser from call sites intended to work on browser.  This is working for customer scenarios, but the `dotnet/runtime` repo itself isn't currently producing warnings for the scenario.

Since support for browser is not implied, the analyzer requires an MSBuild item for `<SupportedPlatform Include="browser" />` to be supplied in order for browser-related warnings to be produced.  With #41760, we enabled the analyzer in the master branch, but a quick test [during the review of that PR](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/41760#issuecomment-689255604) revealed that even with this MSBuild item specified, the errors were still not getting produced within the libraries projects.

We need to:

1. [x] Identify which libraries projects should have `<SupportedPlatform Include="browser" />` specified, and annotate them as such, indicating that the library is intended to be supported on browser
1. [x] Ensure that each of those projects can produce warnings/errors from the analyzer during a normal build
1. [x] Resolve any warnings/errors that currently exist with the annotations that have been made

/cc @mdh1418 @steveisok

@mdh1418 @steveisok Question for you...

> Identify which libraries projects should have `<SupportedPlatform Include="browser" />` specified, and annotate them as such, indicating that the library is intended to be supported on browser

Is the correct answer here the following?

* Find assemblies that _do not_ have `[assembly: UnsupportedOSPlatform("browser")]`
* Mark all of those assemblies with `<SupportedPlatform Include="browser" />`

That would mean for all assemblies that have at least partial browser support, that we want to see warnings if we call APIs unsupported on browser without also annotating those call sites.
Makes sense to me.  Seems like the easiest way.

That does seem like the way to go. 
Is it not the case that assemblies by default are assumed to be supported on all platforms unless otherwise specified by either exclusive `Supported` or `Unsupported`? Otherwise, would marking `<SupportedPlatform Include="<platform>" />` need to be done for all platforms that fully/partially support assemblies?

Why enable it for browser only? There are annotations for other configuration as well and all configurations would benefit from additional checks of not using unsupported APIs (e.g. Linux calling Windows only API or Android calling macOS API)

For `Unsupported` APIs the analyzer would warn if the `platform` is included in the default [MSBuild `<SupportedPlatform>`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/master/src/Tasks/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks/targets/Microsoft.NET.SupportedPlatforms.props):
```XML
<Project>
  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- Platforms supported by this SDK for analyzer warnings. Spec: https://github.com/dotnet/designs/blob/master/accepted/2020/platform-exclusion/platform-exclusion.md  -->
    <SupportedPlatform Include="Android" />
    <SupportedPlatform Include="iOS" />
    <SupportedPlatform Include="Linux" />
    <SupportedPlatform Include="macOS" />
    <SupportedPlatform Include="Windows" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```
Or If the project is targeting the `platform` attributed as unsupported, or the `platform` is manually included within the `MSBuild` \<SupportedPlatform> items group

@mdh1418 @steveisok -- @buyaa-n and I were discussing this and we think we can actually apply this attribute even more liberally.  For projects that have `[assembly: UnsupportedOSPlatform("browser")]` specified, it would even be OK to mark those with `<SupportedPlatform Include="browser" />` as every call site in the application would be treated as unsupported on browser, so no diagnostics would be raised for calls into APIs unsupported on browser.

With that, @buyaa-n is intending to take an approach where `<SupportedPlatform Include="browser" />` would be specified for any project while building against `$(NetCoreAppCurrent)-Browser` or `$(NetCoreAppCurrent)`, regardless of whether or not `[assembly: UnsupportedOSPlatform("browser")]` is specified.

Checked the ` Ensure that each of those projects can produce warnings/errors from the analyzer during a normal build` task as the [PR](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn-analyzers/pull/4281) ensuring that is merged

For the 1st task, I have added the `<SupportedPlatform Include="browser"/>` for projects targeting browser and seems it is enough (i think no need to add it for all multitargeted projects if we do that we could get unwanted warnings for any unsupported browser API referenced for non-browser targets ).
```XML
  <ItemGroup Condition="('$(TargetsBrowser)' == 'true' or '$(TargetOS)' == '') and '$(IsTestProject)' != 'true'">
    <SupportedPlatform Include="browser"/>
  </ItemGroup>
```
And found 97 warnings found in System.Net.HttpListener, System.Security.Cryptography.Algorithms and System.Net.Http projects. With a quick review looks most of them referencing APIs having assembly-level `UnsupportedOSPlatform("browser")` but might be supported on the browser. The whole list of warnings attached
[unsupported browser warnings.txt](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/files/5344790/unsupported.browser.warnings.txt)
 

The 3rd task says ` Resolve any warnings/errors that currently exist with the annotations that have been made`, not sure if i should do that because i don't really know how they should be handled, if the warnings supposed to be Asserted  or the referencing APIs should have `SupportedOSPlatform("browser")` attribute added or the call site should have  `UnsupportedOSPlatform("browser")`  attribute added or whatever other action needed

review_comments: Isn't this redundant?
It is using `SemaphoreSlim.Wait()` in 2 APIs, annotating them causing the entire type to be annotated
Why does this need to be suppressed?  Shouldn't the whole call chain be `[UnsupportedOSPlatform("browser")]`?
You can `SendAsync` on `browser`. You just can't `Send`. All the places that call this method with `async == false` already have `[UnsupportedOSPlatform("browser")]` on them.
Ah, I see.
Might better to annotate the entire type `Barrier`

@ManickaP I think it'd be better to split the code instead of passing bool parameter as it will avoid generating async infra code for sync methods and there will be no dependency to sync code from async-only workloads

Why is this method triggering the warning? This is private, not a public API. I also do not see anything from `HttpClient` in the `unsupported browser warnings.txt` mentioned in the description. So I'm wondering why is this even touched?

I'm asking because the whole implementation of sync is based on this. Down the call chain you'll find many more private methods with `bool async` parameter. So fixing it here might not solve anything and just move the problem one layer down.

The warning is triggered by the tool which checks if all code which can possibly throw PNSE is correctly annotated/propagated. The warning fires here correctly because this method can possibly throw PNSE.

We can suppress it like it's done in this PR but we could avoid that if we could propagate the attribute up. This case is interesting because it mixes async and sync code which I think is not ideal because it penalizes the sync version implementation with underlying async infrastructure which could be worth addressing on its own.

So you'd split this into 2 private helpers, with the same body except for two lines of code? I'm wondering how would it look like, how much code duplication would be introduced.

We can try that and see how it looks like and decide whether it's worth it.
Yep, the helpers would actually be quite different in IL because one of them would be of `async ValueTask<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsyncCore` and second one `HttpResponseMessage SendSyncCore`.

> I think it'd be better to split the code instead of passing bool parameter as it will avoid generating async infra code for sync methods and there will be no dependency to sync code from async-only workloads

I disagree.  Splitting the code all the way down will result in _massive_ code duplication, making the code harder to maintain, leading to even larger binary size, and making it much more likely we'll diverge in implementation between the sync and async.  The sync code is there to be a functional alternative when you really can't use async for some reason, and I'm not concerned about the extra async machinery involved on the sync code path when that happens.

> Splitting the code all the way down will result in massive code duplication

It does not look like massive duplication to me if instead of 50 lines you have 75+ including comments (https://gist.github.com/marek-safar/4700253934660069fb0dbe1cbaf4fb00) but happy to leave that to you guys to decide

You're talking about just the HttpClient layer then?  We use this same bool approach throughput SocketsHttpHandler to have a single implementation of HTTP/1.1 that works for both sync and async; that's the bulk of the duplication I was referring to.

The question is: will the split at the `HttpClient` level solve the problem? Won't it just bubble up at another place? And if it solves it, is it worth it (code duplication of one method vs. warning disable)?

Yes, we are talking about this method only (that's why the comment is here) because it's common for all http-handler implementations. In browser-wasm case, it manifests this way but for other implementations it might have size impacts because even if you always use async versions the high-level code pulls sync dependencies as well. 

I think SocketHttpHandler implementation is not relevant here as it's implementation default of the handler and it's just one of the handlers.

@ManickaP Should we just keep this suppression in here for now and file an issue to split this method into Sync/Async methods?
